name: health
title: Health
description: Check that the integration is alive: mints a real access token, reads the order history, and reports the Bolt user id, when the refresh token expires (and whether that is soon), the order count, the latest order, and how many order details are stored locally. Run this before concluding the MCP is broken.

name: list_orders
title: List orders
description: Past Bolt Food orders, newest first: date, local time, restaurant, state. One cheap call, no products. listedPrice is what the app's order list shows; it EXCLUDES the courier tip and is NOT what the card was charged. For amounts that join to a bank row, use get_receipt or match_card_charges.

since.description: First order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

until.description: Last order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

provider.description: Case-insensitive substring of the restaurant name.

state.description: Only orders in this state. Only 'delivered' orders were paid for and kept.

name: get_receipt
title: Get receipt
description: One order as an itemised receipt: every product with quantity, unit and line price, pre-discount price, options and notes; items a grocery picker replaced or removed (adjustment); Bolt's price lines (subtotal, fees, tips, discounts) verbatim; the total; and what each payment method was charged. charged.card is the amount that appears on the bank statement. priceLines are Bolt's display and do not sum to the total. Amounts are decimal strings.

name: get_receipts
title: Get receipts
description: Receipts for every order placed in a date range (at most 93 days). Order details are fetched one at a time, two to three per second, and stored once an order has been final for a week, so only the first read of a range waits on Bolt. An order Bolt will not return is reported as {partial: true} instead of failing the batch.

since.description: First order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

until.description: Last order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

state.description: Only orders in this state. Only 'delivered' orders were paid for and kept.

detail.description: 'headline' = provider, date, total and the card / Bolt Balance split. 'full' = the whole receipt: every product with options and discounts, Bolt's price lines, payments, refunds, notices.

name: match_card_charges
title: Match card charges
description: Pair bank card rows with the Bolt Food orders they paid for, and return each pair with its receipt. Send the rows exactly as the bank booked them, debits negative, each with its currency. A debit pairs with a delivered order when its amount equals the order's CARD leg (the total minus any Bolt Balance used) and the booking date is 1 day before to 2 days after the order's local date; same-amount orders are claimed in time order. Returns matched pairs, debits nothing claimed (not Bolt Food), credits (refunds, which pair with nothing), and card-paid orders inside the charges' date span that no charge claimed. On Romanian statements 'Bolt Services Ro S.r.l.' is Bolt Food; 'bolt.eu/o/...' and 'Payu*bolt.eu' are rides and will not match.

id.description: Your id for the row, e.g. the ledger's transaction id. Echoed back.

date.description: Booking date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

amount.description: Decimal with its sign, as booked: a debit is negative ('-42.50' or '-42,50'). A positive amount is a credit, such as a refund: it is listed under credits and pairs with no order.

detail.description: 'headline' = provider, date, total and the card / Bolt Balance split. 'full' = the whole receipt: every product with options and discounts, Bolt's price lines, payments, refunds, notices.

name: search_items
title: Search items
description: Every product ever ordered, grouped by restaurant and name, most-ordered first: times ordered, quantity, total spent, first and last date, latest unit price. Delivered orders only; removed grocery lines excluded. Needs every order's details: without a date range, the first run on a cold store fetches two to three orders a second, so a long history takes minutes; later runs read the local store.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the product name. Omit to rank everything.

since.description: First order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

until.description: Last order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

name: export_items
title: Export items
description: Write one CSV row per product line (every state, with order id, date, restaurant, prices, discount, options, adjustment) to the server's exports directory and return its path, SHA-256 and size. Needs every order's details: without a date range, the first run on a cold store fetches two to three orders a second, so a long history takes minutes; later runs read the local store.

since.description: First order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

until.description: Last order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

name: order_stats
title: Order statistics
description: What delivered orders cost, per restaurant and per month: orders, paid (every payment leg: card, Bolt Balance, other), card (what the bank statement shows) and the average per order, exact decimals, per currency. byStore lists the restaurants paid the most (store is the restaurant's name, null when Bolt gave none); refunds are not subtracted. Without dates it covers the whole history. Needs every order's details: without a date range, the first run on a cold store fetches two to three orders a second, so a long history takes minutes; later runs read the local store.

since.description: First order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

until.description: Last order date, YYYY-MM-DD, as a calendar date in Europe/Bucharest (inclusive).

top.description: How many stores byStore lists, the most paid first; `stores` counts them all.
